name: Central Khams Tibetan, Trayap / Brag-g.yab variety
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.

catalog_quote: 3.3.1. Stress within words is apparently not phonemically significant. Words of more than one syllable normally have stress on the first syllable, though a rising tone-contour makes it difficult to hear this. Stress is attracted by the heavier of two syllables. A "heavy" syllable is one with a final segment (including /·/ and /-n/). Disyllabic words with two heavy or two light syllables have acoustically about equal stress. The final syllable of trisyllabic words is invariably low in tone-contour, but it is not unstressed. Enclitics are without stress; in transcription they are separated by a space from the word to which they are phonologically bound.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Khams (Brag-g.yab/Trayap variety) is tonal (two phonemic word tones realised as word-level pitch contours, 3.1.1-3.1.4); word stress is non-contrastive. Default: stress on the first syllable of a polysyllabic word; in disyllables of unequal weight the heavy syllable (closed, or with the raising/length co-vowel /·/ or final /-n/) attracts the stress; disyllables of equal weight (both heavy or both light) have roughly equal stress; enclitics are unstressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described; final syllable of trisyllables is low-pitched 'but it is not unstressed'.
new_statements.exceptions: Heavy second syllable attracts stress away from the first; equal-weight disyllables have level stress; rising tone contour obscures initial stress perceptually; enclitic particles and auxiliaries unstressed (and reduced in quantity, 3.2). Cross-dialect caveat from other opened sources: Suzuki 2011 (dGudzong) finds stress 'not phonetically evident'; Suzuki 2012 (mBalhag) optional non-contrastive stress only ever on the first syllable; Suzuki 2013 and Tournadre & Suzuki 2023: 243 report an iambic (weak-strong) prosodic pattern in the sDerong-nJol / some Southern Kham dialects, versus the trochaic pattern of most Kham.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word including bound enclitics (enclitics unstressed, written spaced); based on isolated words and short utterances from one primary speaker (Nyima Dorje, Ranup village, Brag-g.yab, Chamdo) plus three secondary Trayap speakers recorded in exile; sentence stress treated separately in 3.3.2.
new_statements.identity_note: Olson 1974 describes 'Central Khams Tibetan' = the speech of Brag-g.yab (Trayap / Zhag'yab, Chaya County, Chamdo Prefecture, TAR), from refugee speakers recorded outside Tibet whose everyday speech he notes is partly mixed with Central Tibetan; this falls under Glottolog kham1282 (Khams Tibetan) but is one local variety. The corroborating Suzuki sources describe other kham1282 varieties: dGudzong (Danba County, rGyalrong area, Sichuan), mBalhag (Shangri-La, Yunnan), and the sDerong-nJol (Derong-Deqin) group; Hongladarom 1996 and Wang 1996 describe rGyalthang (Zhongdian/Shangri-La). Prosody is not uniform across Khams: most varieties trochaic/first-syllable prominence with word tone, but the sDerong-nJol / some Southern Khams dialects are reported iambic (Suzuki 2013; Tournadre & Suzuki 2023: 243).

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki [鈴木博之]. 2021. カムチベット語察瓦龍 [Tshawarong] 方言の音声記述と語彙 [Phonetic description and vocabulary of the Tshawarong dialect of Khams Tibetan]. アジア・アフリカの言語と言語学 Asian and African Languages and Linguistics 15: 105-137.
tone_statements.quote: Tshawarong 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高平調、上昇調、下降調、上昇下降調の４種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。ただし３音節以上の語の場合、第１、第２音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し、第３音節以降は [22 ] 程度の高さで現れる。 … Tshawarong 方言の声調体系は、語声調で語頭の音節初頭部が高いか低いかの異なりと音節末尾で下降するかしないかの２通りで構成され、計４種の弁別が行われる。
tone_statements.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme in the Tshawarong dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into four types: high-level, rising, falling and rising-falling. They apply with the word as the unit. In words of three or more syllables, however, the distinctive tone pattern is formed over the first and second syllables, and the third and later syllables appear at a height of about [22]. ... The tone system of the Tshawarong dialect is a word tone composed of two parameters, whether the onset of the word-initial syllable is high or low and whether or not it falls at the syllable end, so that four distinctions are made in total.
tone_statements.locator: sect. 3 超分節音, p. 109 (first part) and sect. 6.3 声調, p. 118 (part after the ellipsis); tone marks introduced sect. 2.1, p. 108
tone_statements.summary: Word tone by pitch, four types: high level 55, rising 24, falling 53, rising-falling 243 (high/low onset x final fall or none); set over syllables 1-2, later syllables ca. 22. Nothing on word stress.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki [鈴木博之]. 2015. カムチベット語丙中洛 [Bodgrong] 方言の音声分析 [Phonetic analysis of the Bodgrong (Bingzhongluo) dialect of Khams Tibetan]. アジア・アフリカの言語と言語学 Asian and African Languages and Linguistics 9: 153-193.
tone_statements.quote: Bodgrong 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高平調、上昇調、下降調、上昇下降調の４種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかることが多いが、複合語ではもとの形態素それぞれがもつ声調を保持している場合がる。ただし３音節以上の語の場合、第１、第２音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し、第３音節以降は [22 ] 程度の高さで現れる。 … 初頭子音の性質によって、若干具体的な調値に異なりがあるが、弁別的ではない。 … 声調の型のみによる最小対はほとんど認められない。
tone_statements.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme of the Bodgrong dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into four types: high-level, rising, falling and rising-falling. These mostly apply to the word as a unit, though in compounds each original morpheme sometimes keeps its own tone. In words of three or more syllables the distinctive tone pattern is formed over the first and second syllables, and the third and later syllables appear at about [22] pitch. … Depending on the initial consonant the concrete pitch values differ slightly, but this is not distinctive. … Minimal pairs by tone pattern alone are hardly found.
tone_statements.locator: p. 158, sect. 3 超分節音 with 表４ 'Bodgrong 方言の声調の現れ' (tone marks introduced in sect. 2.1, p. 157)
tone_statements.summary: Four word tones: high level, rising, falling, rising-falling; pattern set over the first two syllables, later syllables low [22]; the fall is often lost non-finally; tone-only minimal pairs rare.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki [鈴木博之]. 2010. カムチベット語瓊波/沖倉 [Khyungpo/Khromtshang] 方言の音声分析とその方言特徴 [Phonetic analysis of the Khyungpo/Khromtshang dialect of Khams Tibetan and its dialectal characteristics]. アジア・アフリカ言語文化研究 Journal of Asian and African Studies 79: 96-120.
tone_statements.quote: Khromtshang 方言の声調は，ピッチの高低による対立で実現され，高平調，上昇調，下降調，上昇下降調の 4 種に分かれる。弁別的なのは現れるピッチの高さ（調値）ではなく，平板か上昇もしくは下降などの型（調類）である。声調は語単位でかかるが，3 音節以上の語の場合，第 1，第 2 音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し，第 3 音節以降は［22］程度の高さで現れる。 … Khromtshang 方言の声調体系は，語声調で語頭の音節初頭部が高いか低いかの異なりと音節末尾で下降するかしないかの 2 通りで構成され，計 4 種の弁別が行われる。
tone_statements.translation: Khromtshang tones are realised by pitch-height oppositions and divide into four kinds: high level, rising, falling, rising-falling. What is distinctive is not the pitch height (tone value) but the type (tone category): level vs rising or falling. Tone applies per word; in words of three or more syllables the first two syllables form the distinctive pattern and later syllables appear at about [22]. … The Khromtshang tone system is word tone built from two choices, whether the start of the first syllable is high or low and whether it falls at syllable end, so four distinctions in all.
tone_statements.locator: sect. 3.1 声調, p. 100 (examples table with 5-scale pitch values p. 101); after ' … ' sect. 6.3.1 声調, p. 112
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Four word tones told apart by contour: high level 55, rising 24, falling 53, rising-falling 132, set over the first two syllables; independent lax (breathy) register per syllable; nothing on stress.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki [鈴木博之]. 2008. ギャロン地域のカムチベット語・丹巴県蒲角頂 [Rongbrag] 方言の音声分析と語彙 / Khams Tibetan Rongbrag [Zhanggu] dialect: phonetic analysis with a wordlist. 国立民族学博物館研究報告 Bulletin of the National Museum of Ethnology 33(1): 39-80.
tone_statements.quote: Rongbrag 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は，ピッチの高低による声調の対立で，高平調，上昇調，下降調，上昇下降調の 4 種の型に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。声調の音声学的な弁別特徴は，語頭および語末におけるピッチの高低である。ただし，3 音節以上の語では，2 音節末のピッチが声調の弁別特徴を担い，3 音節目以降は固有のピッチを担わず，低く平らになる傾向にある。 … 以上に示した調値は，初頭子音によって若干異なりが現れるが，弁別的ではない。声調は型が弁別的に作用すると考えられる。
tone_statements.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme in the Rongbrag dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into 4 types: high-level, rising, falling and rising-falling. They apply to the word as a unit. The phonetic distinctive feature of the tones is the pitch height at word beginning and word end. However, in words of 3 or more syllables the pitch at the end of the 2nd syllable carries the tonal distinction, and the 3rd and later syllables bear no pitch of their own and tend to be low and level. ... The pitch values shown above vary slightly with the initial consonant, but not distinctively. Tone is considered to operate distinctively as a pattern (type).
tone_statements.locator: p. 44, sect. 3 超分節音 (overview also p. 43 sect. 2)
tone_statements.summary: Four word tones: high-level 55, rising 13, falling 52, rising-falling 132, assigned to the whole word; in words of 3+ syllables those after the 2nd are low; onset-conditioned pitch is non-distinctive.

tone_statements.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki [鈴木博之]. 2007. カムチベット語康定・新都橋 [Rangakha] 方言の音声分析 [Phonetic analysis of the Rangakha (Kangding Xinduqiao) dialect of Khams Tibetan]. アジア・アフリカの言語と言語学 Asian and African Languages and Linguistics 2: 131-162.
tone_statements.quote: Rangakha 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高声調と低声調の２種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。 … 声調の音声学的な弁別特徴は、語頭におけるピッチの高低のみであり、語末では一律にピッチが下降する。 … この特徴は、語義弁別には影響を与えない。文の調子すなわちイントネーションの類と考えられる。 … 高声調で単子音の場合は有声音は [44 ] 程度、そうでない場合は [55 ] 程度の高さで始まる。 … 低声調の場合は有声音ならば [13 ] 程度、そうでない場合は [24 ] 程度の上昇形を見せる。ただしいずれの場合も１音節語では下降する。
tone_statements.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme in the Rangakha dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into two kinds, high tone and low tone. They apply to the word as a unit. … The phonetic distinguishing feature of the tones is only pitch height at the beginning of the word; word-finally the pitch uniformly falls. … This feature does not affect lexical distinction; it is considered a kind of sentence melody, i.e. intonation. … In the high tone, with a single initial consonant, voiced initials begin at about [44], otherwise at about [55]. … In the low tone, voiced initials show a rise of about [13], otherwise about [24]. In either case monosyllabic words fall.
tone_statements.locator: sect. 3 超分節音, pp. 133-134 (inventory also at sect. 2.1 p. 133 '声調で２種が認められる。¯：高 ´：低' and sect. 6.3 声調 pp. 141-142)
tone_statements.summary: Two word tones, high and low, contrasting only in pitch height at word onset (high [55]/[44], low rising [24]/[13]); the word-final fall is intonational; simplest tone system among Tibetan dialects.

tone_statements.citation: Haller, Felix. 1999. A brief comparison of register tone in Central Tibetan and Kham Tibetan. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 22(2): 77-97.
tone_statements.quote: In the present paper I would like to discuss register tone in combination with voicing and aspiration. Written Tibetan (WT) forms will be compared with their etymologically corresponding forms in the dialects of Shigatse (Central Tibet) and Bathang (Kham). Register tone may be either high or low in both dialects. [...] The forms of Bathang Tibetan have voiced initials accompanied by high register tone, with the restriction that those forms that go back to WT forms with stop and affricate initials have high register tone in only approximately 73% of the material.
tone_statements.locator: Sect. 1 Introduction, p. 77 and Sect. 4.1, p. 88
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.n_tones: 2 registers (high vs low register tone) in Haller's analysis; Gesang's four ton…

tone_statements.citation: Huang Bufan [黄布凡]. 1995. Conditions for tonogenesis and tone split in Tibetan dialects. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 18(1): 43-62. [English translation (tr. Jackson T.-S. Sun per LTBA practice; translator not verified) of 黄布凡 1994《藏语方言声调的发生和分化条件》民族语文 1994(3): 1-9; paper read at the 26th ICSTLL, Osaka 1993.]
tone_statements.quote: 2.5. Tones carry few associated features, but certain tones are variable and unstable, affecting the overall distinctiveness of tone: The Dege dialect, for example, has four tonemes and six tone values: two long—51 and 131—and two short—55 (53)? and 13 (231). … Certain instances of the 13 (132) tone borne by syllables which had voiced cluster initials vary freely with the corresponding high tones:
tone_statements.summary: Dege Khams: four tonemes, long 51 and 131, short 55 and 13 (variants 53, 231), register set by old initials; some low tones vary freely with high. Yushu: nine phonetic tones reducible to high vs low.

tone_statements.citation: Gesang Jumian [Skal-bzang 'Gyur-med]. 1989. Phonological analysis of Batang Tibetan. Acta Orientalia Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 43(2-3): 331-358. Budapest: Akadémiai Kiadó. [English version of the author's 1984 Central Institute of Nationalities mimeograph Zangyu Batanghua yinxi fenxi.]
tone_statements.quote: 4.1. Toneme class and toneme value. Batang Tibetan has four tonemes (the fifth is the “light tone” of unstressed syllables). 4.1.1. High even (high long) tone (55): … falling (high short) tone (53): … 4.1.3. Low rising (low long) tone (13): … rising-falling (low short) tone (23): … 4.2.1. Historically the four Batang tonemes can be divided according to two kinds of opposition. One of them is the opposition of the old voiced and voiceless initials which determines the high or the low pitch. … The other reflects the old finals which determine long or short quantity …
tone_statements.summary: Four tonemes on every full syllable: high level 55, high falling 53, low rising 13, low rising-falling 23 (register from old initial voicing, length from old finals); tone sandhi in compounds.

sources.citation: Olson, Robert F. 1974. Central Khams Tibetan: a phonemic survey. Kailash: A Journal of Himalayan Studies 2(3): 217-227.
sources.quote: 3.3.1. Stress within words is apparently not phonemically significant. Words of more than one syllable normally have stress on the first syllable, though a rising tone-contour makes it difficult to hear this. Stress is attracted by the heavier of two syllables. A "heavy" syllable is one with a final segment (including /·/ and /-n/). Disyllabic words with two heavy or two light syllables have acoustically about equal stress. The final syllable of trisyllabic words is invariably low in tone-contour, but it is not unstressed. Enclitics are without stress; in transcription they are separated by a space from the word to which they are phonologically bound.
sources.note: Sect. 3 'Suprasegmental phonemes' (tone, quantity, stress). Sect. 3.3.1 p. 225: word stress not phonemically significant; polysyllables normally stressed on the first syllable; stress attracted to the heavier of two syllables (heavy = closed or with final /./ or /-n/); two-heavy or two-light disyllables have about equal stress; final syllable of trisyllables low in contour but not unstressed; enclitics unstressed. 3.1.1: two phonemic tones (high/low), four phonetic pitch levels, word-level contours. 3.3.2: sentence stress remarks only.

sources.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki. 2011. Phonetic analysis of dGudzong Tibetan: the vernacular of Khams Tibetan spoken in the rGyalrong area. Bulletin of the National Museum of Ethnology 35(4): 617-653. doi:10.15021/00003880
sources.note: Sect. 2.4 Tonemes, p. 627: four distinctive pitch patterns functioning as word tone over the first two syllables (later syllables atonal); 'Except for pitch tone, suprasegmental features such as a stress and a phonation type are not phonetically evident.' No stress-placement rule.

sources.citation: Hongladarom, Krisadawan. 1996. Rgyalthang Tibetan of Yunnan: a preliminary report. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 19.2: 69-92.
sources.note: p. 71: four tonemes (55, 13, 231, 51); allotone 11 replaces the rising pitch on the first syllable of disyllables and 'also occurs in unstressed syllables'; grammatical morphemes carry no tone. No statement of where word stress falls.

sources.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki. 2013. Khams-Tibet-go sDerong-nJol (Derong-Deqin) hoogengun no syo-hoogen ni okeru zyakukyoogata no inritu tokutyoo to bunsetuon ni mieru sono han-eikei [Prosodic feature as an iambic pattern attested in dialects of the sDerong-nJol group of Khams Tibetan and its reflexes on segments] (in Japanese). RIHN Descriptive Linguistics Series 5: 1-15.
sources.note: Sect. 2 (pp. 2-3): dialects of the sDerong-nJol (Derong-Deqin, S Khams, Yunnan/Sichuan) group basically have a 'weak-strong' (iambic) prosodic feature realised as segmental weakening of the first syllable; exceptionally some dialects (e.g. mBalhag) have a 'strong-weak' (trochaic) feature usually realised as actual stress on the first syllable; prosodic features apply only to the first two syllables of the phonological word and are explicitly non-phonemic. Sect. 4 (p. 9) quotes the mBalhag stress passage and states stress does not function phonologically.

sources.citation: Suzuki, Hiroyuki. 2012. Kamu-Chibetto-go Shangri-La-ken mBalhag hoogen no hoogen tokuchou [Dialectal characteristics of the mBalhag dialect of Khams Tibetan, Shangri-La County] (in Japanese). Bulletin of the National Museum of Ethnology 37(1). hdl:10502/4929
sources.note: Sect. 2.2 Suprasegmentals, p. 58: four word-tone patterns over syllables 1-2; in polysyllabic words pronounced in isolation an auditorily clear stress may fall on the FIRST syllable (then following syllables realised low-level); stress on the second or later syllable is never observed; stress is non-contrastive and in free variation, so not transcribed. (Japanese: 第1音節に聴覚印象として明瞭な強勢が置かれる例が存在する…第2音節以降に強勢が置かれる例は認められない…強勢の実現は…対立が認められず，かつ自由変異.)

sources.citation: Wang, Xiaosong. 1996. Prolegomenon to Rgyalthang Tibetan phonology. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 19.2: 55-67.
sources.note: p. 65: four tones as in Lhasa (55, 51, 231, 13); 'No tonal marks are given to unstressed words'; short vowels of first syllables whispered/reduced in disyllables. Silent on stress placement.

tone.quote: Tshawarong 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高平調、上昇調、下降調、上昇下降調の４種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。ただし３音節以上の語の場合、第１、第２音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し、第３音節以降は [22 ] 程度の高さで現れる。 … Tshawarong 方言の声調体系は、語声調で語頭の音節初頭部が高いか低いかの異なりと音節末尾で下降するかしないかの２通りで構成され、計４種の弁別が行われる。
tone.locator: sect. 3 超分節音, p. 109 (first part) and sect. 6.3 声調, p. 118 (part after the ellipsis); tone marks introduced sect. 2.1, p. 108
tone.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme in the Tshawarong dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into four types: high-level, rising, falling and rising-falling. They apply with the word as the unit. In words of three or more syllables, however, the distinctive tone pattern is formed over the first and second syllables, and the third and later syllables appear at a height of about [22]. ... The tone system of the Tshawarong dialect is a word tone composed of two parameters, whether the onset of the word-initial syllable is high or low and whether or not it falls at the syllable end, so that four distinctions are made in total.
tone.summary: Word tone by pitch, four types: high level 55, rising 24, falling 53, rising-falling 243 (high/low onset x final fall or none); set over syllables 1-2, later syllables ca. 22. Nothing on word stress.

sources.quote: Bodgrong 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高平調、上昇調、下降調、上昇下降調の４種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかることが多いが、複合語ではもとの形態素それぞれがもつ声調を保持している場合がる。ただし３音節以上の語の場合、第１、第２音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し、第３音節以降は [22 ] 程度の高さで現れる。 … 初頭子音の性質によって、若干具体的な調値に異なりがあるが、弁別的ではない。 … 声調の型のみによる最小対はほとんど認められない。

tone.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme of the Bodgrong dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into four types: high-level, rising, falling and rising-falling. These mostly apply to the word as a unit, though in compounds each original morpheme sometimes keeps its own tone. In words of three or more syllables the distinctive tone pattern is formed over the first and second syllables, and the third and later syllables appear at about [22] pitch. … Depending on the initial consonant the concrete pitch values differ slightly, but this is not distinctive. … Minimal pairs by tone pattern alone are hardly found.

sources.quote: Khromtshang 方言の声調は，ピッチの高低による対立で実現され，高平調，上昇調，下降調，上昇下降調の 4 種に分かれる。弁別的なのは現れるピッチの高さ（調値）ではなく，平板か上昇もしくは下降などの型（調類）である。声調は語単位でかかるが，3 音節以上の語の場合，第 1，第 2 音節までで弁別的な声調の型を形成し，第 3 音節以降は［22］程度の高さで現れる。 … Khromtshang 方言の声調体系は，語声調で語頭の音節初頭部が高いか低いかの異なりと音節末尾で下降するかしないかの 2 通りで構成され，計 4 種の弁別が行われる。

tone.translation: Khromtshang tones are realised by pitch-height oppositions and divide into four kinds: high level, rising, falling, rising-falling. What is distinctive is not the pitch height (tone value) but the type (tone category): level vs rising or falling. Tone applies per word; in words of three or more syllables the first two syllables form the distinctive pattern and later syllables appear at about [22]. … The Khromtshang tone system is word tone built from two choices, whether the start of the first syllable is high or low and whether it falls at syllable end, so four distinctions in all.

sources.quote: Rongbrag 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は，ピッチの高低による声調の対立で，高平調，上昇調，下降調，上昇下降調の 4 種の型に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。声調の音声学的な弁別特徴は，語頭および語末におけるピッチの高低である。ただし，3 音節以上の語では，2 音節末のピッチが声調の弁別特徴を担い，3 音節目以降は固有のピッチを担わず，低く平らになる傾向にある。 … 以上に示した調値は，初頭子音によって若干異なりが現れるが，弁別的ではない。声調は型が弁別的に作用すると考えられる。

sources.note: Four word tones: high-level 55, rising 13, falling 52, rising-falling 132, assigned to the whole word; in words of 3+ syllables those after the 2nd are low; onset-conditioned pitch is non-distinctive.

tone.quote: Rongbrag 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は，ピッチの高低による声調の対立で，高平調，上昇調，下降調，上昇下降調の 4 種の型に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。声調の音声学的な弁別特徴は，語頭および語末におけるピッチの高低である。ただし，3 音節以上の語では，2 音節末のピッチが声調の弁別特徴を担い，3 音節目以降は固有のピッチを担わず，低く平らになる傾向にある。 … 以上に示した調値は，初頭子音によって若干異なりが現れるが，弁別的ではない。声調は型が弁別的に作用すると考えられる。

tone.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme in the Rongbrag dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into 4 types: high-level, rising, falling and rising-falling. They apply to the word as a unit. The phonetic distinctive feature of the tones is the pitch height at word beginning and word end. However, in words of 3 or more syllables the pitch at the end of the 2nd syllable carries the tonal distinction, and the 3rd and later syllables bear no pitch of their own and tend to be low and level. ... The pitch values shown above vary slightly with the initial consonant, but not distinctively. Tone is considered to operate distinctively as a pattern (type).

sources.quote: Rangakha 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高声調と低声調の２種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。 … 声調の音声学的な弁別特徴は、語頭におけるピッチの高低のみであり、語末では一律にピッチが下降する。 … この特徴は、語義弁別には影響を与えない。文の調子すなわちイントネーションの類と考えられる。 … 高声調で単子音の場合は有声音は [44 ] 程度、そうでない場合は [55 ] 程度の高さで始まる。 … 低声調の場合は有声音ならば [13 ] 程度、そうでない場合は [24 ] 程度の上昇形を見せる。ただしいずれの場合も１音節語では下降する。

sources.note: Two word tones, high and low, contrasting only in pitch height at word onset (high [55]/[44], low rising [24]/[13]); the word-final fall is intonational; simplest tone system among Tibetan dialects.

tone.quote: Rangakha 方言で弁別的な超分節音素は、ピッチの高低による声調の対立で、高声調と低声調の２種に分かれる。それらは語単位でかかる。 … 声調の音声学的な弁別特徴は、語頭におけるピッチの高低のみであり、語末では一律にピッチが下降する。 … この特徴は、語義弁別には影響を与えない。文の調子すなわちイントネーションの類と考えられる。 … 高声調で単子音の場合は有声音は [44 ] 程度、そうでない場合は [55 ] 程度の高さで始まる。 … 低声調の場合は有声音ならば [13 ] 程度、そうでない場合は [24 ] 程度の上昇形を見せる。ただしいずれの場合も１音節語では下降する。

tone.translation: The distinctive suprasegmental phoneme in the Rangakha dialect is a tonal opposition by pitch height, divided into two kinds, high tone and low tone. They apply to the word as a unit. … The phonetic distinguishing feature of the tones is only pitch height at the beginning of the word; word-finally the pitch uniformly falls. … This feature does not affect lexical distinction; it is considered a kind of sentence melody, i.e. intonation. … In the high tone, with a single initial consonant, voiced initials begin at about [44], otherwise at about [55]. … In the low tone, voiced initials show a rise of about [13], otherwise about [24]. In either case monosyllabic words fall.
tone.summary: Two word tones, high and low, contrasting only in pitch height at word onset (high [55]/[44], low rising [24]/[13]); the word-final fall is intonational; simplest tone system among Tibetan dialects.
tone.says: Two word tones, high and low, contrasting only in pitch height at word onset (high [55]/[44], low rising [24]/[13]); the word-final fall is intonational; simplest tone system among Tibetan dialects.

sources.citation: Haller, Felix. 1999. A brief comparison of register tone in Central Tibetan and Kham Tibetan. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 22(2): 77-97.
sources.quote: In the present paper I would like to discuss register tone in combination with voicing and aspiration. Written Tibetan (WT) forms will be compared with their etymologically corresponding forms in the dialects of Shigatse (Central Tibet) and Bathang (Kham). Register tone may be either high or low in both dialects. [...] The forms of Bathang Tibetan have voiced initials accompanied by high register tone, with the restriction that those forms that go back to WT forms with stop and affricate initials have high register tone in only approximately 73% of the material.

sources.note: Bathang (Batang) Khams has a high vs low register tone. sources.quote: 4.1. Toneme class and toneme value. Batang Tibetan has four tonemes (the fifth is the “light tone” of unstressed syllables). 4.1.1. High even (high long) tone (55): … falling (high short) tone (53): … 4.1.3. Low rising (low long) tone (13): … rising-falling (low short) tone (23): … 4.2.1. Historically the four Batang tonemes can be divided according to two kinds of opposition. One of them is the opposition of the old voiced and voiceless initials which determines the high or the low pitch. … The other reflects the old finals which determine long or short quantity …
